summary: Zillow addresses the business problem of automatically generating accurate floor plans from dense indoor 360-degree panoramas to enhance home shoppers’ spatial understanding by detecting and localizing wall features like windows, doors, and openings (WDOs). The intended users are home buyers relying on floor plans for room scale and flow insights. The solution involves training supervised object detection models directly on leveled equirectangular panorama images—accounting for projection distortions by focusing bounding boxes on horizontal (left/right) boundaries—to identify three custom-defined classes of WDOs aligned with floor plan needs rather than typical visual definitions. A dedicated dataset of roughly 10,000 annotated panoramas was created with strict annotation guidelines and consensus-building among annotators to ensure consistency despite inherent labeling ambiguities. Zillow experimented primarily with Single Shot Multibox Detector and Faster R-CNN models, finding that training directly on panoramas without spherical convolution modifications yielded promising results close to human performance in detecting doors and windows, though openings remain more subjective. The expected outcome is reliable, automated WDO detection integrated into Zillow’s floor plan generation pipeline, enabling precise room shape reconstruction from panoramic imagery to improve the home-shopping experience.

summary: Picnic’s data science team addressed the business problem of balancing delivery efficiency with customer satisfaction by improving the accuracy of drop time predictions—known as service completion time—in their vehicle routing model for grocery deliveries. Intended for logistics planners and delivery operators, the solution leveraged numerous features from customer, order, regional, and runner data, including proxies like address density to estimate complex variables such as building floor level, while using a robust Huber loss function to mitigate anomalies in the timestamp data. After exploratory analysis and model comparisons, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) was deployed, achieving about a 30% error reduction in test conditions. A pilot test showed a 20% increase in deliveries per trip with only a 2% drop in on-time performance, demonstrating the model’s effectiveness in optimizing the trade-off between operational efficiency and the tight 20-minute customer delivery windows. Following a staged rollout with adaptive safety buffers, the MLP now runs in production across Picnic’s hubs in the Netherlands and Germany, enabling dynamic tuning of efficiency versus punctuality per location.

summary: Dailymotion faced the business problem of automatically categorizing videos across more than 20 languages using textual metadata (title, tags, description) to enhance content recommendation for millions of users, with existing models limited to English and French. To address the Zero-Shot cross-lingual classification challenge without requiring costly hand-labeled data or translation, they applied cross-lingual Transfer Learning leveraging multilingual pre-trained NLP models (m-BERT, XLM, MUSE) that produce embeddings in a shared vector space. After extensive testing on complex, real-world video metadata differing from typical NLP benchmarks and considering content distribution variance per language, they found that MUSE, emphasizing aligned embeddings across languages and offering faster computation via lightweight CNN-based architecture, outperformed heavier Transformer-based models like m-BERT and XLM in Top-1 accuracy and practical efficiency. The final solution involves encoding multilingual metadata via MUSE embeddings fed into a deep neural classifier, enabling automatic video category predictions at upload in production, with plans to integrate additional modalities such as computer vision for further catalog improvement.

summary: LinkedIn addresses the business challenge of scaling generative AI (GenAI) applications for complex, long-running tasks such as recruitment assistance by building multi-agent AI systems that think, plan, and act collaboratively with human-in-the-loop control to ensure safety and trust. Their solution targets recruiters and members by extending an existing tech stack with modular, scalable GenAI agents defined through gRPC service schemas and orchestrated via a messaging system that enables reliability and parallel task execution. Important constraints include ensuring privacy, security, observability, and user experience across asynchronous, multi-device interactions, supported by tooling for developer experimentation, memory management, and layered observability with LangSmith and OpenTelemetry. This approach yields proactive, personalized, adaptive AI agents capable of autonomous yet user-aligned workflows, improving task efficiency and user engagement while maintaining control and explainability.

summary: The business problem addressed is the persistent challenge of managing duplicate issues and overloaded backlogs in large team workflows, affecting engineers and support teams who risk redundant work and inefficiencies. The proposed AI-driven solution leverages large language models (LLMs) to generate semantically accurate vector embeddings of issue content, enabling cosine similarity searches to detect related or duplicate issues during the issue creation process, triage, and customer support integrations. Embeddings and metadata such as status, workspace, and team identifiers are stored in a partitioned PostgreSQL database using the pgvector extension to ensure scalability and performant similarity queries among tens of millions of issues. This semantic retrieval system integrates closely with Linear's workflow and existing platforms like Intercom, helping users surface and consolidate similar issues proactively, reducing manual aggregation and improving backlog management accuracy and response efficiency.

summary: Thomson Reuters addressed the challenge of providing timely, accurate customer support in specialized legal and tax domains by implementing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system, combining dense vector retrieval of domain-specific knowledge-base content with a GPT-4 seq-to-seq model. Customer support agents, burdened by cognitive overload due to vast, evolving data across CRM and knowledge articles, gained a chat interface fetching precise, contextually relevant resolutions from curated databases via embeddings indexed in a vector database (Milvus). This hybrid parametric–non-parametric approach mitigated GPT-4’s hallucination issues and ensured provenance by grounding responses in up-to-date documents, ultimately reducing ticket resolution times and better meeting growing customer service expectations.

summary: GetYourGuide addresses the challenge of managing and optimizing millions of travel-related images sourced from partners, tour providers, and travelers to enhance customer visual experiences across product and marketing channels. Users include internal teams such as branding and marketing as well as travelers. The proposed solution involves an AI-driven image lifecycle: moderated and safe-for-work images are deduplicated through hashing, then annotated with computer vision techniques—including external APIs (Google Vision) and custom classification models—to capture relevant content and company-specific concepts. Image similarity detection is enhanced beyond pixel comparison by extracting feature embeddings via EfficientNet and employing Facebook AI Similarity Search (FAISS) to identify and filter near-duplicate images, thereby maintaining content diversity especially for marketing use. Constraints include context-specific content moderation and efficient storage management, while the expected outcome is an optimized, diverse, and brand-aligned image repository that improves traveler engagement and marketing effectiveness.

summary: eBay addresses the challenge of providing personalized recommendations across its massive, dynamic inventory of over two billion listings to hundreds of millions of users by developing Mercury, an agentic AI platform that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and a Listing Matching Engine. Mercury structures LLM tasks as modular "Agents," enabling scalable, reusable, and autonomous workflows that transform unstructured data into relevant personalized item suggestions. By combining in-context learning with continuously updated domain-specific data—including live eBay listings, user interactions, and external web sources—Mercury ensures recommendations are contextually accurate and timely. The Listing Matching Engine maps LLM-generated text outputs to live inventory through advanced text-to-listing retrieval, anomaly detection, filtering, and personalized ranking, optimizing for low latency and quality trade-offs. Mercury also incorporates AI safety measures such as content moderation and prompt injection prevention to maintain responsible usage. This solution enhances eBay’s recommendation systems at industrial scale, delivering a robust, scalable, and maintainable AI-powered shopping experience that dynamically adapts to evolving user preferences and marketplace trends.

summary: LinkedIn Learning addresses the business problem of delivering hyper-personalized course recommendations to over 690 million members, including 23 million paid subscribers and large enterprises, to help users develop relevant professional skills and increase platform engagement. Intended users are individual learners with diverse backgrounds and levels of prior interaction on the platform. The proposed solution employs a scalable recommendation engine composed of two complementary machine learning models: Response Prediction, which uses user profile features and course metadata to predict explicit engagement and performs well for new or less active learners; and Collaborative Filtering, which leverages implicit engagement data (e.g., course watches) to learn latent user and course representations, excelling with active users but suffering from the cold start problem. These models’ recommendations are blended dynamically in an online system architecture, combining offline computation with contextual real-time adjustments and A/B testing frameworks, while continuously incorporating new content and user data. The expected outcome is highly relevant, personalized course suggestions that enhance user skill development and platform activity, supported by a robust, scalable infrastructure serving millions globally.

summary: Kingfisher addressed the challenge of extracting meaningful insights from large volumes of unstructured customer feedback across multiple retail banners by developing a scalable, automated semantic retrieval pipeline combining Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), BERTopic with contextual BERT embeddings, and a neural network to project model topics into a human-labelled topic space. This solution leverages unsupervised topic modeling to automatically detect themes in survey responses, enhanced by large language models (LLMs) via few-shot learning to efficiently generate annotated data and reduce manual labeling effort by over 90%. The hybrid approach overcomes limitations of individual models by integrating statistical word co-occurrence, contextual semantic understanding, and supervised guidance, allowing business users—such as customer experience analysts—to rapidly explore latent themes, monitor topic trends over time by location, and derive actionable customer insights that support data-driven improvements in loyalty programs, store layouts, and app features, ultimately driving customer retention and revenue growth.

summary: Zillow addresses the challenge of helping home shoppers efficiently find suitable properties amid nearly 50 available search filters by introducing Guided Search, which offers personalized search refinements as limited UI buttons. These refinements are ranked based on probabilistic models leveraging clickstream data, accounting for the user's current filter selections and regional search context to suggest the most relevant filters that reflect local preferences and user behavior patterns. The solution treats refinement suggestion as a ranking problem predicting the likelihood a user will click a given filter, using co-occurrence and sequential filter-change events in different models to capture both simultaneous and stepwise filter usage, with fallback mechanisms depending on data availability. Early A/B testing in select regions shows a 33% increase in filter engagement and improvements in downstream business outcomes like home saves and agent contacts. Future directions include incorporating a broader set of property attributes and unstructured data, enabling machine-learned ranking models that refine the personalized search experience and help customers discover homes aligned with their preferences more intuitively.

summary: Haleon addresses the business problem of extracting actionable insights from multilingual consumer queries on its health brands by leveraging NLP-based semantic retrieval techniques aimed at their Consumer Relations team and product strategists. The solution processes two years of timestamped, de-identified social media query data in five languages, translating non-English content, and applying text normalization steps like stop word removal, lemmatization, and stemming before generating TF-IDF-weighted uni- and bi-grams. Queries are then semantically categorized via fuzzy matching to stakeholder-driven keywords, enabling trend analysis across products, languages, and geographies through a Power BI dashboard. This enables Haleon to identify evolving customer needs, safety concerns, unmet demands, and emerging market opportunities in real time, ultimately driving data-informed innovation, marketing strategies, and enhancing customer satisfaction while adhering to Responsible AI guidelines.
